The game is complete and syntactically valid. **`snake_ollama-qwen3.8-flash-next-125b-a6b-q4_01.html`** (813 lines, ~28 KB, fully self-contained — just open it in a browser).

**What's implemented:**

- **30×30 grid** rendered on a 600×600 canvas (20px cells, subtle grid lines, responsive CSS scaling), dark theme with glowing food and rounded snake segments.
- **Continuous movement** — game loop ticks every 110 ms; each snake moves in one of 4 directions and grows +1 when eating its food (red apple for snake 1, orange for snake 2); food respawns only on free cells.
- **Collision rules** — hitting a wall, any body segment (own or opponent's), or a head-to-head crash ends the game; the surviving snake wins, simultaneous death is a draw.
- **Keyboard controls** — Player 1: WASD, Player 2: Arrow keys. 180° reversals are blocked; inputs are queued (up to 3) so fast presses register.
- **CPU mode** — BFS pathfinding to its food avoiding walls and snake bodies (own tail treated as passable since it moves away); if no path exists, it falls back to a safe move (preferring straight, then random safe).
- **Three game modes** — Human vs Human, CPU vs Human (P1 = CPU 1, P2 = human), CPU vs CPU. Selectable via menu buttons or number keys 1/2/3.
- **Live score HUD** — both player names and scores shown above the canvas, updated on every meal.
- **Start menu** with title, mode buttons, and control hints; **game over screen** showing the winner and final scores.
- **Restart keys** — `R` returns to the menu, `Enter` replays the same mode; `Space`/`P` pauses.

I verified the inline JavaScript parses cleanly with Node (`new Function` check passed after all edits), and reviewed the full game logic (tick order, collision handling, CPU AI, state transitions) directly in the source.

{"path":"snake_ollama-qwen3.8-flash-next-125b-a6b-q4_01.html","edit_description":"Create a single-file Snake game (HTML + CSS + JavaScript inline) with these exact requirements:

1. Classic Snake on a 30x30 grid, rendered on an HTML5 canvas (cell size ~20px, canvas 600x600, responsive scaling via CSS max-width).
2. Snakes move continuously (game loop with setInterval/requestAnimationFrame tick, ~110ms per step). Each snake moves in one of 4 directions (up/down/left/right).
3. Two snakes play simultaneously (player 1 and player 2). Food items: one per snake (e.g. red apple for snake 1, blue/orange for snake 2). When a snake eats food, it grows by 1 segment and its food respawns at a random free cell; score increases.
4. Collision rules: a snake dies if its head hits a wall (outside 30x30 grid) or hits any body segment (its own or the other snake's). When a snake dies, the game ends and the OTHER snake wins; if both die on the same tick it's a draw.
5. Keyboard controls: Player 1 uses WASD (W/A/S/D), Player 2 uses Arrow keys. Reverse-direction input is ignored (can't turn 180 degrees). Input is queued so quick presses register.
6. CPU-controlled snake mode: an AI that automatically searches for food using BFS pathfinding on the grid to its food, avoiding walls and snake bodies (treat other snake body as obstacle, own body as obstacle except tail cell which will move away). If no path to food exists, it picks any safe adjacent move (prefer the one maximizing free space / following its tail). Must be robust and never crash.
7. Three game modes selectable from the start menu: "Human vs Human", "CPU vs Human", "CPU vs CPU". In CPU vs Human, player 1 is CPU and player 2 is human (or label clearly which side is CPU). In CPU vs CPU both are AI.
8. Score displayed during gameplay: show both snake names/scores (length or points) in a HUD above the canvas, updated live.
9. Start menu overlay: title "SNAKE", mode buttons (3 modes) plus keyboard hints (WASD for P1, arrows for P2, SPACE pause, R restart). Clicking a mode starts the game.
10. Game over screen overlay: shows winner ("Player 1 Wins!", "Player 2 Wins!", "CPU Wins!" etc. depending on mode), final scores, and "Press R to restart" (restart goes back to menu) and also allow Enter to replay same mode. Pressing R or Enter while on game over screen works.
11. Pause with SPACE or P during play (show "PAUSED" overlay).
12. Nice styling: dark theme, centered layout, subtle grid lines on canvas, rounded snake segments, glowing food, modern fonts, styled buttons with hover effects. Clean, well-organized, commented code.

Use colors: snake 1 green (#4ade80), snake 2 cyan/orange (#38bdf8 or #fb923c). Background dark (#0f172a), canvas slightly lighter (#1e293b) with grid lines.

Make sure the file is fully self-contained, works by opening in a browser, no external resources. Name players according to mode (e.g. "CPU 1"/"Player 1"/"Player 2"/"CPU 2")."}
